entries.title: Macaulay Culkin Reveals 'Idea' for "Home Alone "Sequel with Kevin Facing Off Against His Son: 'He's the One Setting Traps'
entries.snippet: Macaulay Culkin, now 45, reflected on and shared an idea for a potential sequel to the 1990 holiday classic *Home Alone* during his “A Nostalgic Night with Macaulay Culkin” tour celebrating the film’s 35th anniversary in Long Beach, California. While not entirely against the idea of reprising his iconic role as Kevin McCallister, Culkin emphasized that the concept would need to be "just right." He proposed a storyline wherein Kevin, now a widower or divorcee and working too hard, is estranged from his son, who ends up locking him out and setting traps—reversing the roles from the original films. Culkin described the house in the story as a metaphor for their damaged relationship. He added a humorous personal detail, revealing that his own sons, whom he shares with fiancée Brenda Song, don’t recognize him in the *Home Alone* films. Meanwhile, original director Chris Columbus expressed doubts about reviving the franchise, suggesting its unique charm shouldn’t be replicated.

entries.title: "Home Alone" Director Chris Columbus Says This Iconic Scene Was a 'Complete Accident' - and Macaulay Culkin's Idea
entries.snippet:
In a recent interview with The Hollywood Reporter's Awards Chatter podcast, “Home Alone” director Chris Columbus revealed that the film’s iconic "aftershave" scene—where Macaulay Culkin’s character Kevin McCallister places his hands on his cheeks and screams—was a spontaneous accident rather than a scripted moment. Originally, Culkin was instructed to touch his face briefly before screaming, but he held his hands there, prompting laughter from the crew and ultimately staying in the film due to its strong positive reaction from audiences.

Columbus credited Culkin entirely for the memorable shot and expressed his admiration for the actor’s natural talent. He also reflected on casting decisions, including pairing Daniel Stern with Joe Pesci after initial casting missteps, which led to undeniable onscreen chemistry. Columbus shared his hopes of working with Culkin again, although he clarified it wouldn't be for another "Home Alone" movie. Additionally, Culkin recently joked about nearly buying the real-life "Home Alone" house but opted out due to family commitments.

entries.title: Here's Macaulay Culkin's idea for a 'Home Alone' sequel
entries.snippet:
Macaulay Culkin, now 45, shared his idea for a potential "Home Alone" sequel during his "A Nostalgic Night with Macaulay Culkin" tour commemorating the film's 35th anniversary. In his proposed concept, Culkin envisions playing an older Kevin McCallister who is either a widower or divorcee, raising a child who becomes upset with him. The twist: Kevin is locked out of his house, and instead of battling burglars, his own son sets traps against him.

While Culkin expresses openness to a sequel under the right conditions, "Home Alone" director Chris Columbus cautions against revisiting the classic, stating it was a unique moment that shouldn't be reproduced. Culkin humorously recounted personal stories from the original film, including an incident where co-star Joe Pesci bit his finger during rehearsal, leaving a lasting scar. He also mentioned that his own children, Dakota and Carson, are unaware he played Kevin in the film, though they have begun mimicking the trap-setting antics.

Despite other attempts to revive the franchise, including a Disney+ reboot in 2021, Culkin's idea stands out as a heartfelt and modern spin on the original storyline.

entries.title: 'Home Alone' McCallister kids reunite for the first time in over 30 years - with one notable exception
entries.snippet:
More than three decades after the release of the beloved 1990 holiday classic "Home Alone," several McCallister family cast members gathered for a rare reunion — but Macaulay Culkin, who famously played Kevin, was notably absent. The nostalgic meet-and-greet took place at Pandora's Box Toys & Collectibles in Lafayette, New Jersey, featuring Kristin Minter, Michael C. Maronna, Devin Ratray, Angela Goethals, and Jedidiah Cohen, all of whom portrayed Kevin's siblings or cousins in the film. It marked their first collective reunion in over 30 years.

While Culkin was missing, he recently spoke fondly about his children enjoying the film, with his 3-year-old son Dakota even believing he once was Kevin. Culkin was also seen earlier this month reuniting with Catherine O’Hara, who played his mother, during his Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony. Ratray shared in 2021 that castmates have stayed loosely connected via a group chat, keeping the "Home Alone" spirit alive.
